review_text:
There is a lot to get used to, yeah i am a RoR2 player, did play a bit of 1 but did not play much after a single decent run. I am keen on giving it another chance with this though. 

The pixel work and animations are beautiful. It was really brought into modern pixel creativity and quality

The stuff to get used to: 
-You take a lot more damage all the time with almost no way to mitigate through movement and you do a lot less damage unless you get meta items or find coveted group killing items. 5s to kill a single enemy and you get overwhelmed FAST so you really have to pick battles and concentrate the enemies who can traverse for multi-hit/pierce skills. 
-Firing is a valuable commodity, your speed is halved when attack on most survivors so you can't run and gun, attributes heavily to doing less damage but i can see kiting would be a cheese strat 
-Unless i am completely missing things the item count is really barren especially in the first stage, likely to find just one outside the boss. 
-In RoR2 you could rush easier with portal particles since you could see across the map, you have to get ready to get unlucky finding the portal
-drones are significantly worse as they will float in melee range but looks like you can pay more to get them back.
notes: - A Risk of Rain 2 player keen to give the first game another chance.
- Beautiful pixel work and animation, brought up to modern quality.
- You take much more damage with little way to avoid it by moving, and deal far less - five seconds to kill one enemy - so you are overwhelmed fast.
- Most characters move at half speed while attacking, so you cannot run and gun.
- Items are scarce, especially on the first stage - often just one besides the boss.
- Unlike Risk of Rain 2, you cannot see the teleporter from across the map, so finding it is luck.
- Drones are much worse - they float into melee range - though you can pay to get them back.

review_text:
[h2]Pros:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Straight forward controls
[*] Unique characters
[*] Brutal RNG
[*] Fun the play with friends
[*] Banger soundtrack
[*] Fantastic pixel graphics
[/list]

[h2]Cons:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Some characters feel glossed over
[*] Some abilities feel not fully fleshed out at times
[*] Brutal RNG
[*] Too many loops feel too punishing at times
[/list]

[h2]Intro[/h2]

I didn't 100% the original Risk of Rain (got to 93%), and Steam hasn't even fully logged all of the play hours (208.8 hours) due to me playing with mods like Starstorm. I can definitely say from experience that this is a definite upgrade from the original. Much of the gameplay is th$
I can't wish enough luck to the guys at Hopoo and their future endeavors.
To Gearbox, you will 100% take the Hopoo gang for granted, and that frustrates me beyond belief. I would hope at the very least you take notes from them and give them the respect they deserve. If I find out you haven't, then I'll just add that to the list of reason I find Gearbox...[i]disappointing[/i], to say the least.

[h2]Review[/h2]

If you liked Risk of Rain 2, you might not like this game. Both OG and Returns are much more difficult, as you have one less axis of movement to dodge enemies. That's not to say RoR2 is bad (although Gearbox has certain made a few hiccups in recent past to make it not as enjoyable), but it's a different experience.

Artificer is probably one of the more if not the most disappointing thing about this game. In RoR2 she was quite a bit of fun to play, albeit overpowered at times, but her primary and utility abilities are extremely lackluster. OG RoR had a mod for Artificer that was better.

The other thing is some alternate abilities need a lot more getting used to or just make it to where you need more specific items to feel useful with the rest of the characters kit.  [spoiler]Bandit's alt primary and Enforcer's alt ult/special come to mind.[/spoiler]

Other than that, this is a great remake of the OG game.
notes: - A definite upgrade from the original, from a player with over 200 hours in it, partly modded.
- Brutal luck - listed as both a pro and a con.
- Some characters feel glossed over - Artificer most of all, her primary and utility lacklustre.
- Some alternate abilities are not fleshed out or need specific items to be useful.
- Too many loops feel too punishing.
- Risk of Rain 2 players may not like it: one less axis to dodge in makes it harder.
- Fears Gearbox will take the studio's team for granted.

This game, at launch, lead to one of the worst malding sessions I have ever had. For the first couple of hours i played, I was having a fair enough amount of fun, and then I got into the later providence trials. I then multiple hours on ONE specific HAN-D trial.. and could barely beat it, much less get any progress towards a golden ranking. Discouraged, I remember going to sleep, and not touching the game for four months. I even made a grand return to playing ror2!
But, a friend of mine decided to 100% the game, and they had been at it all this time. With the aiming update, a handful of patches, and several providence trials being re-balanced, I decided to get back into it.
This game is truly incredible. From the music, to the story, to the game-play, every aspect of this game was enjoyable. The process to complete this game, isn't. To earn all the achievements and get another perfect game on your profile is relatively easy, and fun enough. There are still challenges, and none of them (as of current patch) are 'too difficult'. None of the achievement unlocks are like that damned HAN-D trial.
The unlocks that don't unlock achievements are fun to find as well. I have several now, some I found naturally, and others I had to look up and go 'wow yeah I wasn't figuring that out'. Collecting every log is gonna be a pain, but an inevitability if I keep playing the game. As a bonus, I got a golden rank on every providence trial. In fact, the last 7-10 hours of game play I've done were exclusively providence trials.
Now all that's left is to finish the rest of the game, read all the logs, and dream of wells and worms. Good-ish game, and an amazing series.
notes: - At launch one HAN-D trial took hours and drove them away for four months.
- The aiming update, patches and rebalanced trials brought them back.
- The music, story and play are all enjoyable.
- The achievements are now reasonable - none too hard on the current patch.
- The unlocks that are not achievements are fun to find, some only by looking them up.
- Collecting every log will be a pain.
- Got a gold rank on every Providence Trial; their last 7-10 hours were all trials.
